title: Before the sun goes down
tomorrow: what's the last prayer before the lights go out?

cards: Orange light on the side of a building. Shadows stretching across a parking lot. Sundown has a look and a temperature: the air cooling on bare arms, the streetlights flickering on.
A letter to the Ephesians uses it as a clock. Not a phone alarm. The sky.

teach.h: BE YE ANGRY, AND SIN NOT.
teach.b: Here's the line, in the King James Bible: “Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath.” It moves in steps. Be angry: the anger itself isn't condemned.
Sin not: what's done with it is what matters.
Then the deadline: sundown. The next verse adds, “Neither give place to the devil.” A grudge kept overnight gives something worse room to settle in.
Someone is at the altar with a gift and remembers a brother has something against him: “Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother.” Even worship waits.
And the Lord's Prayer, which some Christians pray morning, noon and night, puts it in every day: “forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.”
Forgiving isn't pretending nothing happened, and it never means staying where someone keeps hurting you. Some wounds take far longer than one evening.
But a small offense, a sharp word, a slammed door, can often be set down tonight, even if the full conversation waits. The light going is the deadline arriving.

how: Some Christians, including some married couples, try to settle a quarrel before going to sleep, often citing Ephesians 4:26, and some forgive someone by name in their night prayers.

games.q: what does “before the sun goes down” mean?
o: saying evening prayers at the moment of sunset
settling small angers before the day is over
finishing the day's chores before it gets dark

games.q: anger and the clock — tap the pairs.
p: let not the sun go down upon your wrath

s: the Bible says all anger is a sin
be ye angry, and sin not: the anger itself isn't condemned.
Jesus says to leave your gift at the altar and be reconciled first
it's setting an offense down, and never means staying where someone keeps hurting you.

games.q: your roommate ate your leftovers again, and you're steaming. it's 9 p.m. what fits Ephesians 4:26?
o: say nothing and stay annoyed; being angry is the sin anyway.
wait a week so you can make the strongest case.
name it calmly tonight, or set it down, before you sleep.
games.why: be angry: the anger isn't condemned. sin not, and don't let the sun go down on it.

practice: Turn toward the nearest window or light and watch it for a moment as if it were the sun going down.

Close your hands around one small sting from today, a sharp word or a slight, then slowly open them and let it rest in your open palms. If you pray, you can say the line from the Lord's Prayer: as we forgive our debtors.

wordCard.voice: Before the sun goes down. Settling small offenses as the day ends, so anger doesn't spend the night.

orig.note: the Greek behind wrath in Ephesians 4:26: anger that has been stirred up.

carryVoice: Keep this: nothing carried to bed, because the sky sets the deadline. Day 1691, settled.
